questions.question: In branch prediction architectures, what is the primary operational advantage of a 2-bit saturating counter (bimodal predictor) over a simple 1-bit predictor?
options: It allows tracking global branch correlations across distinct branch instruction addresses.
It prevents a single anomalous branch outcome (such as the final exit of an inner loop) from immediately altering the next prediction.
It eliminates the need for a Branch Target Buffer (BTB) by directly encoding branch target addresses.
It avoids all pipeline stalls by computing both paths speculatively in parallel.
It halves the storage requirement of the pattern history table.

questions.question: In deep-submicron digital IC design, how does cross-coupling capacitance (Cc) between two adjacent parallel signal interconnects affect propagation delay when both nets switch simultaneously in opposite directions (one transitioning low-to-high, the other high-to-low)?
options: The coupling capacitance has negligible effect because the complementary voltage swings cancel each other out.
The effective coupling capacitance is eliminated, resulting in a substantially faster signal transition on both nets.
The effective coupling capacitance is approximately doubled due to the Miller effect, significantly increasing propagation delay on both nets.
Only the net with the stronger driver experiences an increased delay, while the weaker net accelerates.
The dynamic voltage rail collapses momentarily, causing static subthreshold leakage to dominate the delay profile.

questions.question: In weakly ordered memory consistency models (such as those adopted in ARM, RISC-V, and modern standard multithreading specifications), what fundamental memory ordering guarantee is provided by a load operation with 'Acquire' semantics?
options: No subsequent read or write operations in program order can be reordered before the Acquire load.
All prior write operations in program order must be globally visible before the Acquire load can be executed.
The Acquire load executes atomically with an immediate subsequent store to the same memory address.
No prior read or write operations in program order can be reordered after the Acquire load.
The Acquire load forces an immediate cache flush and broadcast invalidation to all other coherent cores.

questions.question: In advanced sub-7nm FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAA) nanosheet technologies, why has the Self-Heating Effect (SHE) emerged as a critical reliability and performance concern compared to legacy planar bulk CMOS?
options: Metal gate stacks exhibit dramatically higher electrical resistivity than polysilicon, generating intense localized resistive heating.
FinFET gate oxide layers are made substantially thicker, preventing heat from transferring into the gate electrode.
Operating supply voltages (VDD) have risen above 1.5 V to maintain switching speeds, quadratically increasing active power density.
Confined three-dimensional silicon channel geometries enclosed by low-thermal-conductivity dielectric materials severely impede heat dissipation.
Sub-threshold swing degrades below ideal physical limits, causing runaway static leakage currents during switching.

questions.question: In modern DDR DRAM memory controllers, what is the core operational principle of the First-Ready First-Come-First-Served (FR-FCFS) request scheduling policy?
options: It strictly services memory requests in chronological arrival order, prioritizing write bursts over read bursts to maximize write buffer draining.
It rotates priority equally across all available DRAM banks in a strict round-robin manner to eliminate thread starvation.
It prioritizes requests originating from the core with the highest instruction throughput to maximize system IPC.
It batches all write requests into a dedicated queue that flushes exclusively when the memory bus enters a low-power state.
It prioritizes requests targeting an already opened DRAM row buffer (page hit) over older pending requests requiring row activation or precharging, breaking ties using arrival time.
